domain_invariants.requirement: A sensor has a unique positive id, an existing owner user, a unique serial matching ^[A-Z0-9-]{6,32}$, a name of 1..80 characters, and type TEMPERATURE, HUMIDITY, CO2, or ILLUMINANCE.
A sensor type has an immutable physical value range: TEMPERATURE -50.0..150.0 Celsius, HUMIDITY 0.0..100.0 percent, CO2 0..5000 ppm, and ILLUMINANCE 0..200000 lux.
A reading is immutable, belongs to exactly one existing sensor, has a positive id, a value within that sensor physical range, and a captured_at UTC ISO-8601 timestamp with second precision.
For a sensor, captured_at is unique; duplicate readings at the same timestamp conflict rather than overwrite historical telemetry.

A sensor can have at most one active threshold policy. Its optional lower_bound and upper_bound are within the sensor physical range, at least one is present, and lower_bound is strictly less than upper_bound when both exist.
Writing a reading atomically evaluates the active threshold policy and creates exactly one immutable alert when the value is below lower_bound or above upper_bound; otherwise it creates no alert.

A telemetry range uses a half-open UTC interval [from,to), where from is earlier than to and the interval is no longer than 31 days; returned readings are ordered by captured_at ascending and then id ascending.
Sensor deletion is forbidden while any reading, threshold policy, or alert refers to it; readings and alerts are never independently updated or deleted.
An alert stores the triggering reading value, bound direction BELOW or ABOVE, and the policy bounds effective at creation; changing or deleting a policy never changes earlier alerts.
A user may access only sensors and derived telemetry owned by that user; an admin may access every sensor. Private routes deny access by default.

seed_data: Deterministic local users exist with ids 1 and 2 in role user and id 3 in role admin; authentication is a valid non-expired server-side Bearer session and no token value is exposed.

All timestamps are UTC ISO-8601 with second precision. Every list returns items and next_after_id, uses ascending immutable numeric id order unless REQ-2-007 specifies a temporal order, accepts limit 1..100 default 20 and optional after_id > 0, and returns null next_after_id when exhausted.

Every private route is deny-by-default. Invalid JSON is 400; POST and PATCH bodies require application/json and otherwise are 415; syntactically or structurally invalid inputs are 422. Local persistence unavailability is 503 and unexpected local failure is 500 with no partial write.

apis.formal_requirement: The system shall expose GET /health as a public endpoint with no input or authorization, returning deterministic local persistence health without persistent effects; it shall emit only 200 or 503.

The system shall expose GET /sensors as an authenticated user-or-admin endpoint accepting optional type enum, serial_prefix of 1..32 uppercase serial characters, owner_id for admins only, limit, and after_id; it shall apply exact type, normalized prefix, and owner filters, enforce REQ-2-010, use stable pagination, make no persistent changes, and emit only 200, 401, 403, 404, 422, 500, or 503.

pseudocode.body:
FUNCTION handleListSensors(request):
    // REQ-2-012; Preconditions: local persistence is available.
    REQUIRE authenticated user or admin; otherwise RETURN 401.
    VALIDATE filters, limit, and after_id; RETURN 422 if invalid. IF supplied owner_id <= 0 OR absent THEN RETURN 404. END IF
    IF caller is user AND owner_id names another user THEN RETURN 403. END IF
    READ only caller-owned sensors for user, or filtered sensors for admin; order by id and page; RETURN 200.
    // Transaction: none. Postcondition and all error paths leave sensors, readings, policies, and alerts unchanged; RETURN 500 or 503 only for local failures.

apis.formal_requirement: The system shall expose POST /sensors as an admin-only endpoint accepting application/json owner_id, serial, name, and type; it shall validate REQ-2-001, require a positive existing owner_id, reject a duplicate serial, atomically create the sensor without derived relations, be non-idempotent, return 201 with Location, and emit only 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 415, 422, 500, or 503.

pseudocode.body:
FUNCTION handleCreateSensor(request):
    // REQ-2-013; Preconditions: JSON body and available persistence.
    REQUIRE authenticated admin or RETURN 401/403; REQUIRE application/json or RETURN 415; parse JSON or RETURN 400.
    VALIDATE REQ-2-001; RETURN 422 if invalid. IF owner_id <= 0 OR owner absent THEN RETURN 404. END IF
    BEGIN TRANSACTION. IF serial exists THEN ROLLBACK; RETURN 409. END IF
    CREATE sensor; COMMIT; RETURN 201 with Location.
    // Non-idempotent. On every error rollback; sensor, readings, policy, and alerts remain unchanged.

apis.formal_requirement: The system shall expose GET /sensors/{sensor_id} as an authenticated owner-or-admin endpoint accepting a positive path id; it shall authorize under REQ-2-010, return the sensor and current policy summary without modifying state, treat non-positive or absent ids as 404, and emit only 200, 401, 403, 404, 500, or 503.

The system shall expose PATCH /sensors/{sensor_id} as an admin-only endpoint accepting application/json with one or both of name and owner_id; it shall validate the non-empty patch, REQ-2-001, and a positive existing owner_id, atomically update only supplied fields without transferring or deleting telemetry relations, be idempotent for an identical valid payload, and emit only 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 415, 422, 500, or 503.

The system shall expose DELETE /sensors/{sensor_id} as an admin-only endpoint accepting a positive path id; it shall atomically delete a sensor only when it has no readings, policy, or alerts, shall not cascade-delete telemetry, be non-idempotent after success, return 204, and emit only 204, 401, 403, 404, 409, 500, or 503.

The system shall expose GET /sensors/{sensor_id}/thresholds as an authenticated owner-or-admin endpoint accepting a positive path id; it shall return the optional active policy, make no persistent changes, treat non-positive or absent sensor ids as 404, and emit only 200, 401, 403, 404, 500, or 503.

The system shall expose POST /sensors/{sensor_id}/thresholds as an authenticated owner-or-admin endpoint accepting application/json lower_bound and/or upper_bound; it shall validate REQ-2-002 and REQ-2-005 against the sensor type, reject an existing policy, atomically create one policy, be non-idempotent, return 201 with Location, and emit only 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 415, 422, 500, or 503.

The system shall expose PATCH /sensors/{sensor_id}/thresholds as an authenticated owner-or-admin endpoint accepting application/json with at least one supplied lower_bound or upper_bound; it shall validate the complete resulting policy under REQ-2-005, atomically update only supplied bounds without rewriting alerts, be idempotent for an identical valid payload, and emit only 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 415, 422, 500, or 503.

The system shall expose DELETE /sensors/{sensor_id}/thresholds as an authenticated owner-or-admin endpoint accepting a positive path id; it shall atomically delete only the active policy, retain all readings and alerts unchanged, be non-idempotent after success, return 204, and emit only 204, 401, 403, 404, 500, or 503.

The system shall expose POST /sensors/{sensor_id}/readings as an authenticated owner-or-admin endpoint accepting application/json value and captured_at; it shall validate the positive existing sensor, REQ-2-002 through REQ-2-006, reject a duplicate captured_at, atomically create one reading and any required alert, be non-idempotent, return 201 with Location, and emit only 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 415, 422, 500, or 503.

The system shall expose GET /sensors/{sensor_id}/readings as an authenticated owner-or-admin endpoint accepting a positive path id, optional from and to UTC timestamps, limit, and after_id; it shall apply inclusive from and exclusive to filters to captured_at, validate REQ-2-007 when both timestamps are supplied, use stable id pagination, make no persistent changes, and emit only 200, 401, 403, 404, 422, 500, or 503.

The system shall expose GET /readings/{reading_id} as an authenticated reading-owner-or-admin endpoint accepting a positive path id; it shall return the immutable reading after sensor ownership authorization, make no persistent changes, treat non-positive or absent ids as 404, and emit only 200, 401, 403, 404, 500, or 503.

The system shall expose GET /sensors/{sensor_id}/latest as an authenticated owner-or-admin endpoint accepting a positive path id; it shall return the most recent reading by captured_at then id or null when none exists, make no persistent changes, and emit only 200, 401, 403, 404, 500, or 503.

The system shall expose GET /sensors/{sensor_id}/range as an authenticated owner-or-admin endpoint accepting a positive path id and required from and to UTC timestamps; it shall enforce REQ-2-007, return matching readings and deterministic minimum, maximum, average rounded to four decimal places, and count, make no persistent changes, and emit only 200, 401, 403, 404, 422, 500, or 503.

The system shall expose GET /alerts as an authenticated user-or-admin endpoint accepting optional sensor_id, direction enum BELOW or ABOVE, resolved boolean, limit, and after_id; it shall validate optional sensor existence and filters, restrict users to alerts derived from their sensors, use stable pagination, make no persistent changes, and emit only 200, 401, 403, 404, 422, 500, or 503.
